answer: Biological provenance logging. Each agent identity is tied to a physical sensor trace whose unique pigment signature is recorded as a cipher at enrollment; the enforcement rule rejects any identity whose sensor history shows duplicated or synthetic traces, since forging a plausible pigment record requires real time in a physical environment. An attacker must therefore occupy a distinct physical haven per identity and sustain genuine sensor exposure, making each fake identity cost roughly one hardware unit plus weeks of continuous real-world presence rather than a payment.
